closed_schools: North Star Elementary — closed end of 2024-25 (consolidated into East/Main).
Larsen Bay School — closed 2018 (<10 students); building transferred to the village in 2022.
Karluk School — closed 2 Nov 2023 (students moved to AKTEACH).
Danger Bay School — in 2015-16 SABS but not in NCES 2024-25; treated as closed.
mil_not_placed: Little Navy / NSGA Chiniak (1954 Navy communications/DF site) — no reliable coordinates; described in the Miller Field card sources but not placed.
Bald Hill (Site 3) distant-electrical-control bunker and St. Peter's Head 8-inch guns — no coordinates found; covered in the Fort J.H. Smith card.

travel_not_included.Harvey Flying Service: Only a very old web page found (mentions ERA Aviation terminal); no evidence it is still operating — left off.

properties.name: Fort J. H. Smith (WWII coast artillery)
properties.label: Fort J. H. Smith (WWII coast artillery)
properties.rows: What it wasWWII Army harbor-defense fort at Cape Chiniak / St. Peter's Head. Battery No. 1 mounted 8-inch guns at St. Peter's Head with a two-story underground ready-ammunition bunker. A gas-proof plotting/fire-control switchboard bunker (completed 24 Dec 1943) sits about 1,400 ft south of the 8-inch emplacement, with phone cables to the guns and Miller Field.Dates1942–WWII (plotting bunker completed 24 Dec 1943)UnitsCoast artillery; Battery G (searchlight), 250th Coast Artillery, per veteran accountWhat remainsGun emplacement/ammo bunker on the hill across the lagoon, plotting bunker, searchlight/control shelters (as of kadiak.org 1998–2000 visits).AccessOn Leisnoi Inc. land east of the end of state road maintenance — check 17(b) easements / Leisnoi permit rules. Bunkers can hold standing water.Coordinates57.62420, -152.19482Location confidencemedium — Point is the GNIS reference for the fort as a whole, not a specific gun.SourcesGNIS 'Fort J H Smith (historical)' via KIB geographic names layer; kadiak.org (Kodiak Military History Museum site, Joe Stevens) chiniak/command, chiniak/chinmap, units pages
properties.note: Old military sites can hold hazards (open bunkers, debris). Respect private/Native land.

properties.name: Miller Field (WWII airstrip) & Chiniak DGPS
properties.label: Miller Field (WWII airstrip) & Chiniak DGPS
properties.rows: What it wasWWII Army airstrip of steel Marston matting serving the Chiniak defenses. The Coast Guard installed a differential-GPS transmitter (313.0 kHz) beside the runway c. 1997. Navy families used nearby quonsets as a recreation area from 1956.DatesWWII; DGPS c. 1997UnitsU.S. Army (WWII); USCG (DGPS)What remainsPotholed runway with partly removed Marston mat — NOT usable for aircraft (1998). UAF SuperDARN radar sits across the runway (not military).AccessReached from the end of the Chiniak Hwy; Leisnoi land — check easements.Coordinates57.61429, -152.19594Location confidencehighSourcesOSM way 641205098 (abandoned runway 'Miller Field'); kadiak.org (Kodiak Military History Museum site, Joe Stevens) chiniak tour (1998); Chiniak Area Comprehensive Plan 1987 (chiniak.org)
properties.note: Old military sites can hold hazards (open bunkers, debris). Respect private/Native land.

properties.name: Chiniak Air Force Tracking Station
properties.label: Chiniak Air Force Tracking Station
properties.rows: What it wasStarted 1956 as a USAF Aircraft Control & Warning (AC&W) site; converted in 1958 to a satellite tracking station collecting tracking/telemetry data (linked to the CORONA reconnaissance satellite program per kadiak.org).DatesConstruction 1956; operational 1960; closure announced March 1975UnitsUSAF (2 officers) with ~121 civilian contractor staff (Philco-WDL / Philco-Ford)What remainsBuilding foundations/structures and the tracking-station dam (NID AK00086) nearby.AccessPrivate/Native corporation land — permission or easement required.Coordinates57.59811, -152.17988Location confidencemediumSourcesOSM way 238396430 ('Kodiak Tracking Stations'); OSM dam way 1241500320; kadiak.org (Kodiak Military History Museum site, Joe Stevens) af_track pages; Chiniak Area Comprehensive Plan 1987
properties.note: Old military sites can hold hazards (open bunkers, debris). Respect private/Native land.

properties.name: Cape Greville fire-control station / CG radio beacon
properties.label: Cape Greville fire-control station / CG radio beacon
properties.rows: What it was40-acre harbor-defense site (acquired 29 Aug 1941) for the B3/2 fire-control station spotting for the 155 mm battery at Chiniak Point. Dug-in reinforced-concrete 'cottage' observation post completed Sept 1942 (M1 depression position finder). Commissioned April 1943 as a radio and radar-beacon station; turned over to the Coast Guard Oct 1944.Dates1941–1944+UnitsHarbor Defenses of Kodiak; U.S. Navy (Seabees built); USCG from Oct 1944What remainsOP, a small shiplap hut used by campers, a quonset hut (fall 2000).AccessRemote; Leisnoi land — check easements.Coordinates57.59000, -152.15722Location confidencemediumSourceskadiak.org (Kodiak Military History Museum site, Joe Stevens) greville page: 'approximately N57 35 24, W152 09 26'; GNIS Cape Greville
properties.note: Old military sites can hold hazards (open bunkers, debris). Respect private/Native land.

properties.label: 155 mm battery, Chiniak Point (approx.)
